sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (Quality Checks row 45 #44; Internal Quality Checks row 45 annotation; neighbouring #42/#43 and Deterministic check-scoring-policy.py/check-rubric-schema.py rows)
evidence: Static review of frozen task (input_sha256 f3019705...). Workbook 'Quality Checks' row 45 (#44) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 45 (Mukesh: functionality 60 percent, each dimension with its own per-criterion weightage) read via zipfile XML parse; skill references/quality-checks.md section 44 ('real functionality outweighs structure and style; sanity-check maximum contribution of non-functional dimensions'), staged-task-contract.md tests/scoring.toml section, SKILL.md delivery profile (shaped 0.6/0.2/0.2). (1) Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2, [gates] 0.0/0.0, [floors] functional=0.05 -- byte-identical in values to template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/tests/scoring.toml and the frozen profile; score.py computes sum(w*score)/sum(w) and zeroes reward if a gate or the functional floor fails. Functional carries 60 percent; style-only (visual Likert) can contribute at most 0.2. Polish (0.2) is not cosmetic here: its 5 binary rows (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread, hro_pol_earlier_place, hro_pol_failed_send, hro_pol_session_resume) grade draft/focus/scroll preservation under live updates, failed-send recovery and session-expiry draft handling, all stated in instruction.md paragraphs 3-5 and hireops_rules.md lines 122-180. So >=0.8 of reward mass is behavioural. No weight key in any [judge] block (contract line 96). (2) Per-criterion weights: documented scheme comment at scored/functional/judge.toml:23 and scored/polish/judge.toml:17 '1.0 standard, 1.5 important, 2.0 core to the brief (Visual Likert rows are equal)'. Parsed counts (tomllib): functional 44 criteria, sum 61.0, {1:21, 1.5:12, 2:11}; polish 5, sum 9.5, {2:4, 1.5:1}; visual 5 likert points=5 weight 1 each; gates one binary criterion each weight 1 (all_pass, irrelevant). Every 2.0 row maps to what instruction.md names as the hard/central part: hro_refused_put_back ('put the card back where it really is and tell me why'), hro_stale_refused ('tell me who'), hro_bulk_all_or_none ('all of them or none'), hro_undo_restores/hro_undo_conflict ('undo ... as long as nobody has touched those cards'), hro_live_board ('within fifteen seconds without a reload'), hro_thread_earlier ('pull in earlier ones'), hro_unread_counts/hro_unread_scrolled_up ('unread counts need to be right for each person', 'leave my place alone and just tell me'), hro_drafts ('A reply I have not sent stays with that conversation'), hro_candidate_private ('must never see our internal notes ... or anyone else'). 1.0 rows are rules-file details (job/candidate creation validation, role matrix rows, refusal status codes, activity lines, notes, compose details, candidate link) -- still real functionality, appropriately standard. No structural/style criterion in functional or polish. (3) Lessons file check (lesson 2: one documented scheme, no weight steering): git show (read-only) of HEAD/HEAD~1/HEAD~2 functional judge.toml shows previous versions used ad-hoc fractional weights (e.g. 0.12056737, 0.4822695; 145-152 criteria). The frozen candidate replaces them with the single documented 1.0/1.5/2.0 scheme -- this resolves rather than introduces the lesson-2 hazard. (4) Sanity arithmetic: max non-functional contribution = 0.4 of which only 0.2 (visual) is style. Equal-weight sensitivity: an app passing exactly the 21 weight-1 functional rows scores 21/61=0.344 weighted vs 21/44=0.477 equal (reward delta 0.6*0.133=0.08); the skew favours the brief's emphasised concurrency/conversation rules, which is honest but will make the customer audit's 'avg weight of failed vs passed' comparison show failed>passed for a model that misses the hard rows; justified by the public brief, so recorded as a note, not a defect. Floor: functional>0.05 needs >3.05/61 weight (~4 standard rows) before polish/visual count -- floor adequacy belongs to row 43. Effective weight of live push transport spans functional (hro_live_board, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen, hro_msg_exchange ~9/61) and 2 polish rows (4/9.5), ~0.17 reward in total; brief makes live updates central, so this is proportionate (double-penalty adjudication belongs to row 28). Adversarial: a broken app with polished visuals and 4 trivial CRUD rows gets <=~0.24; a correct app with plain visuals gets >=0.8+visual share -- weights don't let style beat function. A conforming alternative is not penalised by weights (weights carry no implementation assumption). No runtime/model measurement exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'); row 44 is a static weight-design check and is not gated on those runs (they belong to rows 42/43), so not counted as missing required evidence for this row.
